chapter: Regional bands, politics and travel abroad
title: Detroit's big organized bands compared with New York
summary: Wilson says Detroit's Greystone Ballroom bands, including the Casa Loma and McKinney's Cotton Pickers, outnumbered New York's.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: Well, that was one of the centers but I think New York was really -- Fletcher Henderson and that group, Duke Ellington around the New York area then, and McKinney's Cottonpickers in Detroit.

And then they had -- all those bands in Detroit organized under Jean Kelte King Goldsap (PHONETIC), that Greystone Ballroom. They'd go in and out of there, broadcast on the road. The Casa Loma Band was there, based there in those days, before Glen Gray was the leader. A guy named Hank Bianint (PHONETIC) fronted them. And Freddie Bergen, the Vagabond, McKinney's Cottonpickers, the Billy Minor Band in Detroit.

Detroit might have had more of those big organized bands, jazz dance bands than any city. They had so many. They had more than New York, because New York had Fletcher and Chick Russel and Charlie Johnson's band. Do you remember those names?
